chunks: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The pregnant woman is divorced with a single divorce.
ai.seo_question: How many divorces are required to finalize the divorce of a pregnant woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the chain of Safwan ibn Yahya, establishing that a pregnant woman is divorced by a single pronouncement (talaqah wahidah) without the need for three distinct utterances. This position is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it contrasts with the majority view of the Sunnis, who generally require three pronouncements for a complete divorce, and highlights the unique application of the waiting period (iddah) for pregnant women as derived from the Quran. The hadith underscores the practical implication that the iddah ends immediately upon childbirth, making the single pronouncement sufficient for the dissolution of the marriage bond.
